subject.title: Rescue: add watchdog core service and cron engine

question: Should OpenClaw core accept an isolated rescueWatchdog cron payload and service-repair mechanism once the current-main contract gaps and proof gap are fixed, or should this stay external/operator-managed for now?
rationale: The patch is a new core recovery capability with service-control and command-execution implications, so correctness fixes alone do not settle the product and security boundary.

options.title: Sponsor core rescue watchdog
options.body: Keep this PR as the candidate but require current-main cron contracts, SQLite persistence, command-job preservation, real-host proof, and secops review before merge.

options.title: Split hardening from watchdog
options.body: Land only narrowly reviewed service/path hardening separately and defer the rescue payload/product flow to a new sponsored design.

options.title: Keep recovery external
options.body: Close or redirect the core rescue payload work and document/operator-manage watchdog recovery outside OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core rescue watchdog
recommendation.body: Keep this PR as the candidate but require current-main cron contracts, SQLite persistence, command-job preservation, real-host proof, and secops review before merge.
